question: Section 3.1 says the filter scores open-loop, so the noise it rejects still builds the state it scores against. Does one refinement iteration that excludes rejected events change the measured separation?
design: Pass A scores at unit weight. Its scores select a keep-mask at the stated retention, using no labels. Pass B re-extracts with weight 0 on rejected events and re-scores. AUC is over all events in both arms, so the comparison is exactly paired within block.
unit_of_analysis: Condition. The 20 conditions are nested in 2 datasets, so the condition-level interval understates the correlation between conditions drawn from the same recording set.
mechanism_caveat: Neither candidate supports an attribution. The saturation coefficient has the wrong sign between conditions, and gate-flip rate separates almost perfectly by dataset, so with 2 datasets its coefficient is an n = 2 contrast.
